title: DN772392 Internal Fire Risk Assessment Repairs
description:
All Housing properties with a shared communal space are subjected to a Type 1 fire risk assessment to comply with the Regulatory Reform Fire Safety Order 2005 (RFO) and the Fire Safety Act 2021. \r
The Council's primary  objective is to keep residents safe by ensuring that they live in homes that comply with fire safety standards. \r
\r
The fire risk recommendations derived from Fire Risk Assessments are assigned risk ratings, which are as follows: critical, high, medium, and low.  Where reasonably practicable, fire safety hazards identified and recorded in the assessment must be completed within the timescales set within the Fire Risk Assessment. \r
\r
To deliver the recommendations, Hackney requires the appointment of a competent and specialist contractor qualified under a recognised scheme, specialising in accredited trades to undertake compartmentation work and ad-hoc fire door replacements.\r
London Borough of Hackney must demonstrate its best endeavours to reduce and mitigate these risks. If Hackney fails to appoint a suitably qualified contractor, it will breach its obligations under the Regulatory Reform Fire Safety Order 2005, Fire Safety Regulations 2021, the Building Safety Act 2022, and the newly introduced tenant satisfaction measures.\r
 \r
This is a direct award opportunity from an existing framework agreement, for the appointment of Sureserve Compliance Fire Ltd to assist Hackney in completing internal reactive fire safety works derived from  fire risk assessments, Including, but not limited to, door upgrades and fire stopping. The contract term is proposed to be a period of 12 months.\r

title: ORAL HEALTH PREVENTION &  PROMOTION SERVICE
description:
The London Borough of Hackney would like to commission Oral Health Prevention & Promotion Service.

Oral Health remains a challenge in Hackney and the impact of Covid-19 has been to increase existing inequalities. Poor oral health disproportionately affects communities who are socially and economically deprived. Oral health is essential to general health and well-being and greatly influences quality of life. Poor oral health is almost entirely preventable.

The new Oral Health Prevention and Promotion service will
achieve better outcomes for residents without increasing resources through more effective targeting and closer partnership working with key stakeholders.

The service will deliver:

Greater awareness of how to maintain good oral health amongst children, vulnerable adults and older people

Improvement in oral health seeking behaviour in local communities
Improved oral health and reduction in dental decay, hospital visits and admissions for tooth extractions

Closer partnership working amongst local stakeholders to improve oral health, including collaborative working with the Local Dental Committee to disseminate information and increase take up of dental services

More effective targeting of the high risk groups such the Orthodox Jewish Community and care home and supported living residents.

The Service is aimed at Hackney and City of London early years and school age children, vulnerable and older adults as well as communities at higher risk of poor oral health.

title: Culturally Sensitive Substance Misuse Support
description:
Person centred, culturally sensitive, support for black people with substance misuse support needs. \r
London Borough of Hackney has seen significant investment in its Substance Use support system since 2021 through successive grant awards made by the Office of Health Improvement and Disparities (OHID). \r
\r
Funding for 24/25 is a part of the Supplementary Substance Misuse Treatment and Recovery Grant (SSMTR). This grant is a continuation and expansion of funding received in 23/24 and totals an approximate £2.9 million for the financial year. \r
\r
As part of the project the Local Authority needs to achieve clear aims in line with national outcomes, including increases in people accessing support services for dangerous and harmful substance use. \r
\r
In previous years the authority has achieved its aims through a programme focussed on underserved communities. This includes older black men, with Culturally sensitive provision provided by Support When It Matters (SWIM). \r
\r
Throughout delivery SWIM has demonstrably increased the number of older black men accessing support for services, and has played a pivotal role in increasing continuity of care from prison discharge into community services as well as providing outreach into areas of the community. This has been successful, and has led to the organisation and authority being included in Central Government best practice recommendations. \r
\r
In 23/24 SWIM piloted a self funded project to address the needs of Black women. Partners across the authority, including probation partners, have reflected the success of this approach through the Combating Drugs Partnership Strategy Group as well as Working Groups. These form key spaces in the governance of the overall substance use support system in Hackney. \r
\r
As part of the submission for the SSMTR the Combating Drugs Partnership, through the strategy group, agreed that a continuation and expansion of the SWIM project was necessary to help further increase the number of black people accessing, and benefitting from, drug treatment services within the authority area. \r
\r
A submission was made to OHID outlining this. OHID have agreed this funding and support the expansion/development of the service to meet the needs of all individuals in the borough who identify as black where there are barriers to accessing the core treatment service.\r
\r
This service falls within the scope of the Public Contract Regulations 2015. Consideration was given as to whether this service should be classified as a rehabilitation service and therefore within the scope of Provider Selection Regime (as a health service provided to an individual) but it was ultimately determined that as an outreach service focusing on a specific community and encompassing a wider range of support than health specific interventions this service should more appropriately be classified as a social work service (CPV code 85320000).

title: General Building Contract 4.1 - Regenerational Voids (interim no.2)
description:
The London Borough of Hackney Estate Regeneration team manages the Council-led direct
delivery of nearly 3,000 new Council homes at 18 sites across the borough, replacing
properties that are uneconomical to repair. These works do not form part of this contract.
The regeneration programme includes 1,300 dwellings within the Woodberry Down and
Colville estates. These dwellings are typically within post war traditional brickwork constructed
low rise blocks of four to six storey height. There are also a few high rise blocks. Colville
Estate has a phased demolition programme over the next 5 years and Woodberry Down
Estate has a demolition programme over the next 10 years.
As existing tenants are relocated from these two estates and if economically viable those
dwellings are made available in the short term (until planned demolition begins) to alleviate
homelessness within the borough. Currently around 130 dwellings are refurbished to the
council lettable standard each year under this scheme. This includes some " Relet voids" being
previously refurbished temporary let properties which as they become vacant are refurbished
and relet again. This contract is for the refurbishment of these void properties.
The void refurbishment works will encompass all general building trades, damp / condensation
works, upvc window repair / replacement, electrical works, including void property rewire.
Scaffolding will be required as incidental in connection with general building repairs. Gas
works, asbestos survey and removal works if required will be carried out by others.
Contractors may at times need to work alongside these specialists. Works will be principally within unoccupied dwellings though some external work may at times be required including
garden clearances. In addition it may at times be necessary to undertake works in occupied
dwellings after voids have been let.

title: DN731976 Lift Modernisation Framework Agreement
description:
Hackney Council Seek to establish a Lift Modernisation Framework of experienced and competent Lift Contractors.

The purpose of this framework is to deliver ambitious annual programmes of work to drive modernisation across the lift stock, by appointing up to three (3) lift contractors to work simultaneously across all regions of Hackney and Hackneys housing stock. The aim is to reduce future maintenance cost and breakdowns and as well as aid in improving the quality of our lift service for our residents and tenants.

Hackney have in excess of 600 lifts within its housing stock. A total of 39 priority lifts have already been identified for renewal. In order to improve the overall percentage of modernisation across the stock, these first 39 lifts form a programme of work that has been included as part of the tender process. Potential bidders will be required to price up a programme that include these 39 priority lifts, as part of their tender commercial submission.
The 39 lifts will be split into 3 programmes of work. Each Bidder appointed to the Framework will be awarded one Year 1 Programme of work in order to front load programme delivery and commence work on site as quickly as possible. The top three scoring Bidders in the tender process will be appointed to the Framework. Following further evaluation of individual programme costs and quality scores, each Framework Contractor will then be awarded one programme of work.
Each contractor appointed to the framework will be allocated a programme of between 11 - 15 lifts for refurbishment, which will effectively form the first 12 month programme of work. Each programme can include any regions and wards across Hackney. Future works programmes will be awarded based on individual contractors' overall performance, initially based on delivery KPIs during the first 9 months.
In addition to the Housing Lift stock, this framework may also include ad hoc lift modernisation and renewal work from other departments across Hackney Council, for example corporate and education buildings.The framework would also allow provision for mini competition if required.
Hackney Council requires experienced and competent lift contractors to be appointed to the Framework. Therefore all Bidders must be a member of a recognised lift industry association such as LEIA (Lift Engineering Industry Association).

Terms
It is anticipated that there will be up to £28,000,000 worth of spend during the full potential term of the framework agreement. It is envisaged that there will be between 18 to 45 lift modernisation projects delivered each year, split across 3 programmes. It is anticipated that each Framework Contractor will be awarded 1 programme of work each year. This will be subject to budget and framework capacity and performance. As such to achieve this ambition, Framework contractors are expected to have the capacity and capability to deliver a minimum programme of 13 lift modernisation projects per annum.

title: City and Hackney: Rough Sleeper's Drug and Alcohol Peer Support
description:
The numbers of people sleeping out on the streets across England hit record levels in 2018, amongst those who sleep out there is a high prevalence rate of problematic and dependent drug and alcohol use. Due to 8 years of central Government underfunding, community drug and alcohol treatment services have been unable to offer the type of enhanced treatment options which achieve better, sustained recovery outcomes for people experiencing homelessness with substance use disorders.

Following the success of Everyone In during the first year of the pandemic in 2020, the Office of Health Improvement and Disparities (OHID), alongside the Department for Levelling Up, Housing and Communities (DLUCH), launched a number of grant funded schemes targeting support for people rough sleeping. The Rough Sleeping Drug and Alcohol Grant is one of these grant funded programmes of work. Most recently this programme has been extended and will run up to the end of March 2025.

The City and Hackney were 2 of the authorities out of 60 in total awarded grant funding. title: NNC- Waste Consultancy Services
description:
North Northamptonshire Council (hereafter referred to as the "Council") is seeking technical advice and support in providing a final report which outlines outcomes and recommendation(s) of what the Household Waste Recycling Centre (hereafter referred to as "HWRC") provision should look like for North Northamptonshire from Tuesday, 1st April 2025.
The Council has identified a requirement for technical support to carry out an Options Appraisal of the current Household Waste Recycling Centre provision for the new authority area of North Northamptonshire, ahead of the end of the current contract arrangements ending Monday, 31st March 2025.
The Options Appraisal will identify the optimal HWRC service provision required to meet the needs of the Council's residents in the near and medium term, whilst meeting its statutory obligations under the Environment Protection Act 1990 (HWRC provision).
The commissioned work will include a final report outlining the recommendations of the most suitable and affordable option based upon detailed analysis of the following list (not exhaustive):
1. In-house or outsourced delivery model - i.e., to include a high-level benchmarking review looking at what other comparable Councils do and how their services perform (recycling performance, customer satisfaction, value for money, and affordability).
2. Identify the optimum location and number of HWRCs to meet future service requirements in accordance with industry standards, best practice, affordability, and the Council's local requirements, (e.g., traffic flows, network pinch points).
3. Review of current opening days and hours to maximise efficiency, increase user/customer satisfaction.
4. Investigate an electronic booking system or other similar options to manage access at peak times and discuss associated benefits (advantages) or detriment (disadvantages).
5. Review current e-permit scheme and recommend other schemes and their benefits.
6. Identify and propose options for the locations of any new/replacement facilities (working on the proviso that two (2) facilities (Kettering and Rushden) have had recent investment and are in good condition and will remain) to complement retained facilities.
7. Support/provide Councillor engagement session(s) to discuss direction of appraisal and likely issues arising.
If you would like to be considered for this contract, please e-mail jo.hackney@northnorthants.gov.uk to request the Request for Quotation document, detailing the Council's requirement and instructions for taking part and responding. Please note the response deadline as no later than 17:00 on Friday, 2nd June 2023.
We would be grateful if you would let us know that you have received this e-mail, and also if you decide not to take part in the competition.
 
We look forward to receiving your submission and in the event of any queries or requests for further information arising from this Request for Quotation, please contact us by e-mail, at jo.hackney@northnorthants.gov.uk.
